newsitem.title: FINLAND: Softer bonds and dollar dent Finnish shares.
newsitem.headline: Softer bonds and dollar dent Finnish shares.

text.p: Shares ended lower on Monday despite cautious early gains as nervous sentiment took the upper hand in the afternoon amid new fears of EMU delay and higher U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
The HEX general index closed 0.56 percent lower at 2,942.53 points and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark ended down 0.65 percent at 1,029.39 points.

Bourse engine Nokia lost 2.50 markka to 316.40, accounting for 25 percent of thin 451 million markka trade. Another quarter of volume was in forestry major UPM-Kymmene which bucked the trend with a 1.10 markka gain to 113.40.

"The clear rise in interest rates and early losses in U.S. stocks sent the market lower," one broker said, adding that the period of uncertainty was likely to continue until Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25.
Nearer term focus for hints of coming U.S. interest rates would be on U.S. February CPI data due on Wednesday, brokers said.

Raision Tehtaat which on Friday announced a joint venture with UPM-Kymmene for technology relating the plant sterol -- the key ingredient in its promising Bencol margarine -- rose sharply to close up 30.00 markka at 490.00.
Consulting group PI-Consulting rose after reporting 1996 earnings back in the black, closing up 3.10 markka at 12.00.
